about: The epistle of the Second Sunday of Advent, from Romans. Paul reads the Scriptures as written for us — so that patience and comfort should breed hope — and ends with a chain of quotations in which the nations praise God together with Israel.

s01.translation: Brethren: Everything that was written was written for our instruction, so that through patience and the comfort of the Scriptures we might have hope.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s02.translation: May the God of patience and comfort grant you to be of the same mind toward one another according to Jesus Christ, so that with one mind and one voice you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s03.translation: Therefore receive one another, as Christ has received you, for the honor of God.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s04.translation: For I say that Christ Jesus became a servant of the circumcised for the sake of God's truth, to confirm the promises made to the fathers; and that the Gentiles are to glorify God for His mercy, as it is written: Therefore I will praise You among the Gentiles, O Lord, and sing to Your name.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s05.translation: And again he says: Rejoice, O Gentiles, with His people.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s06.translation: And again: Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and magnify Him, all you peoples.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s07.translation: And again Isaiah says: There will be a root of Jesse, and He who rises to rule the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will hope.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

s08.translation: May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition
